newsitem.title: USA: CPT says Steel/West Virginia holders nix proposals.
newsitem.headline: CPT says Steel/West Virginia holders nix proposals.

text.p: CPT Holdings Inc said one Thursday that a preliminary count of proxies indicated that Steel of West Virginia Inc's shareholders failed to approve a proposal requiring Steel's board of directors to negotiate with eligible bidders for the company.
CPT, the parent of J & L Structural Inc, has offered $9 a share offer for Steel of West Virginia in a bid to combine that company with J & L. The offer was rejected by Steel of West Virginia.

In a press release, president and chief executive William Remley said, "considering the obstacles that SWVA put in our way, we are not surprised that our proposal requesting that the board of directors negotiate with eligible bidders does not seem to have won approval at this time."
CPT said it would consider taking its bid to shareholders of Steel of West Virginia.

"One of the options we will now consider is to take our proposal directly to stockholders and let them make their interests clear when there is hard cash on the table, rather than wait for SWVA's management to finally agree to negotiate with us in good faith," Remley said in the statement.
CPT said that the preliminary count of proxies also showed that holders had rejected proposals made by the management of Steel of West Virginia.
The three proposals asked for an increase in authorized common stock, the authorization of preferred stock, and the elimination of the right of stockholders to act by written consent.

In a separate release, Steel of West Virginia said that the preliminary tally of votes cast at the annual meeting on Thursday showed that CPT's proposal for negotiations regarding the sale of Steel received support from less that four percent of outstanding shares.

In response to CPT's announcement on Wednesday of a lawsuit against Steel aimed at invalidating its shareholder rights plan, Steel chairman and chief executive Robert Bunting said in the statement that in view of Thursday's shareholder vote, "we can only view this (lawsuit) as an effort to harass the company and divert management's attention from running the business."
